Validate evaluation inputs without building a ledger

tl_validate.Rd

Runs every check that tl_ledger() runs and returns the issues found. Errors stop tl_ledger(); warnings and notes are kept as the issues attribute of the ledger.

Usage

tl_validate(records, reference, predictions, observation = NULL)

Arguments

records

Record table, usually from tl_records(): columns record, start, end, and optionally subject, fs, n_samples.

reference

Reference intervals: columns record, start, end, label. Optional episode gives a physiological episode identifier that is kept when an episode is interrupted, and optional start_sample, end_sample are checked against fs. Target time without a reference row is "unknown".

predictions

Detector responses: columns record, detector, start, end, response ("positive", "negative" or "abstain"). Optional columns: reason (why the detector abstained), issued_at (time the decision became available, used for latency).

observation

Optional input-availability intervals: columns record, start, end, status ("available" or "unavailable"), and optional reason. Uncovered time has status "unknown".

Value

A data frame of issues with columns severity ("error", "warning" or "note"), table, record, row (row number in the input table), issue and detail. It has zero rows when nothing was found.

Examples

fx <- tl_fixture("acceptance")
tl_validate(fx$records, fx$reference, fx$predictions)
#> [1] severity table    record   row      issue    detail  
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
